budget_items.what_was_said: The House Ways and Means budget raised minimum Chapter 70 aid per student from the governor's figure, but a member cautioned this could still change in the Senate and reconciliation.
The House budget fully funded charter school reimbursement at this rate, though a member said that isn't guaranteed to hold.
The House budget proposed this reimbursement rate for required out-of-district placement transportation, prorated based on available funds.
A one-time supplemental appropriations bill drawing on fair share tax surplus was finalized and referred to the Senate.
The supplemental bill raised FY25 regional school transportation reimbursement from the prior rate to full reimbursement.
FY25 circuit breaker reimbursement for out-of-district special education transportation costs was increased from a lower rate.

budget_items.topic: FY26 out-of-district special ed transportation reimbursement
budget_items.what_was_said: The bill separately set a reimbursement rate for FY26 out-of-district special education transportation costs.
The chair said a state representative and the select board chair both reported this amount in earmarks for Lunenburg public schools.
Warrants covering late March to mid-April were presented to the committee for approval.
A donation for STEM supplies at the primary school was recommended for deposit into the school gift account.
An anonymous donation to help students attend Nature's Classroom was recommended for deposit into the Turkey Hill gift account.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: computer purchase/lease to equipment maintenance/lease
budget_items.what_was_said: The transfer was proposed to cover anticipated Canon copier lease and per-copy billing; the business manager said usage caps are being studied but not yet implemented.
A member asked whether the whole line was for network copiers; told it also includes Pitney Bowes postage metering.

budget_items.topic: Transfer: fire safety/furniture repair to vehicle maintenance repair
budget_items.what_was_said: The transfer was requested to cover a deficit in vehicle repair/maintenance for truck and mower repairs through year end.
Money held in the salary reserve line from prior-year bargaining was being dispersed to appropriate salary lines, as is done annually.

Funds were moved into athletic transportation, special detail/events, dues and fees, and high school stipend lines to address a deficit in the athletics revolving account; more reclassification was still expected.
The district switched vendors for Chromebook repair parts after the usual vendor's pricing rose sharply due to tariffs, raising concern about the FY26 budget.
Food service will sell bagged lunches at annual town meeting with several sandwich options, cash only.

budget_items.topic: Potential position restorations from pending state funding
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent estimated that if pending state funding bills all passed, the district could restore about this many positions.
One option discussed was raising the student activity fee to cover advisor stipend costs, with free/reduced-lunch students automatically waived.
Fee calculations were based on the portion of enrollment not eligible for the automatic fee waiver.
A committee member noted the activity fee was set at this amount in 2008, much lower than the current proposal.

budget_items.topic: Municipal building / school district offices project cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The presenter cited the overall project value used in pricing calculations for the town hall, Ritter building and meeting house work.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill full renovation vs. replacement cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The architect estimated the cost to address everything identified in the Turkey Hill study, versus a rough cost to build an entirely new school.
The mechanical engineer said a required fire sprinkler system would cost roughly this amount regardless of which HVAC option is chosen.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill HVAC options cost range
budget_items.what_was_said: The engineer outlined a range of costs across three HVAC strategy options, from a basic repair approach to full electrification.
The outdated electrical system would need to be upgraded no matter which overall option is chosen.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill total study cost estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The total estimate to address everything identified in the report was given, described as less than expected and far less than a new building.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill roof and window costs / MSBA reimbursement
budget_items.what_was_said: The architect gave rough costs for window and roof work and said MSBA reimbursement might cover roughly half if the town pursued the program.
The committee discussed how to prioritize use of free cash for FY26, following up on the prior meeting's conversation.

budget_items.topic: Restoring part athletic director/assistant principal and secretary
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed combining a reduced assistant principal role with athletic director duties and restoring a part-time secretary using free cash.

budget_items.topic: Athletic director salary offset from athletic revolving fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The FY26 budget already offsets part of the athletic director's salary from the athletic revolving account; the superintendent hoped this could balance out as the revolving fund's health improves.

budget_items.topic: Title I and special education federal grants at risk
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said roughly this total in federal Title I and special education grant money was at risk pending a federal certification dispute over DEI practices, and proposed free cash as a backstop.
The green-communities-grant-funded mini-split project at the primary school had a funding shortfall the superintendent proposed covering with free cash.

The superintendent estimated potential unemployment costs from the budget cuts and proposed adding to the existing unemployment budget line with free cash, while expecting the full estimate would not be needed.
A member noted the existing budget already includes an increase intended to help attract a qualified finance/business manager candidate.
Opening additional school choice seats across several grades was projected to generate this much potential revenue the following fiscal year, plus a Chapter 70 effect.
The town manager's warrant article sought to cover FY2025 and prior-year operating deficits, including unanticipated special education move-ins.
The article included funds to decommission portions of the TC Pasios building.
A citizens petition proposition 2½ override question to supplement the school budget was on the warrant; the committee ultimately declined to take a position.

budget_items.topic: Article 12 - Free cash supplement to school operating budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The article would supplement the FY26 school operating budget using free cash, consistent with the earlier discussion.
The parks commission described a scaled-back two-phase project and cited differing per-household cost estimates for the proposed debt exclusion.

budget_items.topic: Article 29 - Municipal building design debt exclusion
budget_items.what_was_said: The total project cost for the Ritter building, town hall and annex renovation, including design fees and contingency, was presented for the debt exclusion article.

decisions.decision: The committee agreed to keep discussing the line-item transfers together rather than voting on each one individually.
The Municipal Building Design Committee presentation was tabled, with no objection, until the presenter arrived on Zoom.
No formal school committee sign-off is required for the summer athletic camps' board of health paperwork; the superintendent will report back once the plan firms up.
The superintendent will revise the FY26/free-cash memo into a town-meeting handout and circulate it to the committee for feedback rather than bring it back for another formal vote.

The committee worked out, with the MASC consultant, that superintendent finalist interviews would be split two per week (week of April 28 and week of May 5), with deliberation on the regular May 7 meeting.

Rather than embedding student questions in the formal committee interview, the two student representatives will coordinate a separate student-led interview block with each candidate during the site-visit day.

minutes.headline: School Committee recommended both town debt-exclusion articles and set FY26 free-cash spending priorities.
minutes.summary: The committee worked through a long warrant-article agenda ahead of annual town meeting, recommending both the Marshall Park and municipal building debt-exclusion questions, the FY25 closeout and capital articles, and the free-cash supplement to the school budget, while declining to take a position on a separate citizens' petition override. It also finalized how to spend free cash to restore several school positions -- including converting the outgoing athletic director's role to part-time combined with an assistant principal -- accepted a draft engineering study on Turkey Hill School's condition and ADA compliance, and worked out interview scheduling for the superintendent finalists.

what_happened.line: The committee voted to recommend both town debt-exclusion questions to town meeting: Marshall Park and the municipal building design.
It also recommended the free-cash supplement to the school operating budget, plus the FY25 closeout and capital articles.
The committee declined to take a position on a separate citizens' petition article to override the town budget for schools.
Free-cash spending to restore school positions was finalized, including combining the outgoing athletic director role with assistant principal duties, part time.
Superintendent finalist interviews were scheduled across two weeks in late April and early May, with deliberation set for May 7.

why_it_matters: The debt-exclusion votes are property-tax questions residents will decide at town meeting and, if approved there, likely at the ballot.
Combining the athletic-director role with assistant-principal duties is a staffing change that affects athletics oversight, including team coordination such as the ski team, per public comment.
Declining to take a position on the citizens' petition override leaves that budget question to town meeting without a School Committee recommendation either way.
